clue.text: Problem of youth, or young boxer out of condition?

parts.note: a young dog of any breed, a boxer included, is a puppy
someone out of condition is flabby, carrying fat

explanation.surface: A question about whether an unfit young fighter's trouble is just adolescence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' suggests a fighter, but it is the dog breed. PUPPY FAT is the plumpness of childhood that most outgrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Childhood plumpness is a common worry of the young, a problem of growing up.

clue.text: Put out old fruit -but it's absolutely fresh

indicators.note: out signals the word Put is knocked out of shape and its letters rearranged

parts.note: a date is the fruit of the date palm

explanation.surface: Someone throws away stale fruit, insisting it was perfectly fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges PUT into UPT. 'old' looks like part of the fruit's description but is O.
explanation.definitionFit: Current and the latest thing; fully fresh news or styles are said to be modern in this way.

clue.text: Showing indulgence for each failure I have

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'per head'
a miss is a failure to hit
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they have been soft each time something went wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A lenient, tolerant attitude allows freedoms, which is showing indulgence.

clue.text: Unreliable pilot in the dark

definitions.meaning: describes an untrustworthy, shady operator or business
read literally, someone who flies by night

explanation.surface: A warning about a pilot who cannot be trusted after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a dodgy operator, and taken literally describes a night flyer.

clue.text: Heavy work — outside broadcast set up for match

indicators.note: outside says the heavy work goes around the other piece

parts.note: a tome is a large, weighty book

indicators.note: set up in a down clue says the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to broadcast seed is to sow it by scattering

explanation.surface: A hefty book and an outside broadcast are arranged for a sporting fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside broadcast' reads as the TV term, but 'outside' is the container signal and 'broadcast' means scattering seed; 'set up' turns it upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of people, like a couple, is a match.

clue.text: One article or two, romantically linked

definitions.meaning: a single thing in a list or collection
a couple seen together as an established romance are called this

explanation.surface: Reading one piece in a magazine, or a pair of lovers.
explanation.definitionFit: A single entry in a list is an item, and a dating couple is informally an item too.

clue.text: Wool to cover up in part of South American state

indicators.note: in says the reversed cover sits inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: Ala is the shortened form of Alabama, a southern American state

indicators.note: up in a down clue reads the cover word upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a cap is a cover, for a head or a bottle

explanation.surface: Someone wraps up warmly in a region of a South American country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' suggests a Latin country, but it is a Southern US state, Alabama, cut to ALA, holding PAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpaca is the fine wool from the llama-like animal of the Andes.

clue.text: Deem vote against party right

parts.note: con is a vote or argument against, as in pros and cons
a side is a party in a dispute or contest

explanation.surface: Someone judges a vote against a party's right wing.
explanation.definitionFit: To deem is to judge or regard, a synonym of think about carefully.

clue.text: One found among battle stations

parts.note: a name that belongs both to a famous battle of 1815 and to a London railway terminus

explanation.surface: Someone discovered at their post during a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battle stations' reads as a military order, but it means a battle that is also a station.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon's final defeat shares its name with a major London rail station.

clue.text: Set aside rivalry, finally, on the floor of the House

parts.note: to store is to set aside for later

indicators.note: finally takes only the closing letter of rivalry

explanation.surface: Parliamentarians put their rivalry behind them in the debating chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floor of the House' suggests the Commons chamber, but it is a level of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A storey is one level of a building, a floor of a house.

clue.text: Lead with others in group from same stable, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Lead and other members of a set come from one stable, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR added a stray S from the next column; the page ends at 'possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead belongs to the class of common non-precious metals alongside iron, copper and zinc.

clue.text: Get beyond usual pointless bid

definitions.meaning: in bridge, the commonest call, which bids nothing

explanation.surface: A card player moves past the ordinary bid that scores nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass is to go past, and at bridge passing is the call that makes no bid.

clue.text: What separates the sides in Animal Farm?

definitions.text: What separates the sides in Animal Farm?

parts.words: What separates the sides in Animal Farm?
parts.note: the ground between trenches, read as a place with no humans, as on Orwell's farm run by animals

explanation.surface: A question about the barrier between factions in Orwell's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: In Orwell's Animal Farm the animals drive out the humans, so the farm is literally free of men.
explanation.definitionFit: The strip between opposing front lines that neither side holds; here punningly a place free of men.

clue.text: Doubly emphatic rejection of a form of purchase

indicators.note: doubly says the rejection word is said twice

parts.note: never is a strong no

explanation.surface: A firm double refusal to buy on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: The NEVER-NEVER is British slang for hire purchase, buying on instalments.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for hire purchase, paying for goods by instalments over time.

clue.text: Does it report soundly on Derby, but not cross-country events?

definitions.text: Does it report soundly on Derby, but not cross-country events?

parts.words: Does it report soundly on Derby, but not cross-country events?
parts.note: a broadcaster heard rather than seen, covering a town such as Derby but not nationwide news

explanation.surface: A question about coverage of a horse race but not of cross-country running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derby' suggests the horse race and 'cross-country' a running event, but Derby is an English city and cross-country means national.
explanation.definitionFit: A town's broadcast station covers its own area by sound, not national affairs.

clue.text: Invest and see big changes coming to East

indicators.note: big changes says the letters of see big are rearranged

explanation.surface: A financier is urged to invest as major shifts reach the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invest' looks financial, but in its military sense it means to surround a town.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest a fortress is the old military sense of surrounding it in a siege.

clue.text: In which one crew is a shade lighter than the other

definitions.text: In which one crew is a shade lighter than the other

parts.words: In which one crew is a shade lighter than the other
parts.note: Cambridge row in light blue and Oxford in dark blue in their annual Thames contest

explanation.surface: A rowing contest where one team weighs a little less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a shade lighter' suggests weight, but it is colour: Cambridge's light blue against Oxford's dark blue.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual Oxford against Cambridge race on the Thames pits dark blue against light blue crews.

clue.text: English chap who puts an end to occupation?

definitions.text: who puts an end to occupation?

parts.note: Victor is a man's name, any chap

explanation.surface: An Englishman who stops people from working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupation' suggests a job, but it means occupying a property.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord who ejects tenants ends their occupancy of the property.

clue.text: Starts at sound of owl in branch

parts.note: the offs are the starts of races
a hoot is the cry of an owl

explanation.surface: Someone is startled by an owl calling from a tree branch.
explanation.definitionFit: A side shoot growing from a plant's stem, or a subsidiary group, is a branch.

clue.text: UK geopolitically restricting uranium, as a rule

indicators.note: restricting says the outer piece hems in the other letter

parts.note: Britain on the world stage is seen as an ally of the United States
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Britain's geopolitical stance limits uranium as a matter of course.
explanation.definitionFit: Normally, generally, in most cases, which is to say as a rule.

clue.text: One who can use multiple media to compose diverse art

definitions.text: One who can use multiple media

indicators.note: to compose is to put together, so these letters are assembled anew

explanation.surface: An artist working in several media creates varied art.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR added a stray K and S from the next column; the page has neither.
explanation.definitionFit: A company promoting itself buys space across print, TV and online, so uses many media.

clue.text: Split in political grouping

definitions.meaning: slang for departed or went away
the socialist and progressive wing of politics

explanation.surface: A rift appears within a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Split means went off, and the left is the progressive political side.

clue.text: Property in relation to beer, say

parts.note: re means regarding, in relation to
ale is a kind of beer
to state is to say

explanation.surface: Someone talks about property and beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example' but is STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Land and buildings are property, called this in the trade.

clue.text: Give biased view on revolution

definitions.meaning: to present news with a slant, as a press officer does

explanation.surface: A political adviser slants the story on an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A press officer puts a slant on events, and a turn of a wheel is a rotation.

clue.text: Divide Oscars, taking some for movies like these

indicators.note: taking some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Share out the Academy Awards among some films.
explanation.definitionFit: Recorded films viewed at home are movies of this format.

clue.text: Local? No, I settled

indicators.note: settled says the letters are placed in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone denies being a native: they moved here and settled.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a colonist settled in a land but was not a local.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonist settled abroad, so is a newcomer rather than a native.

clue.text: Teenager with concealed weapon in seaside resort

indicators.note: concealed says the weapon is hidden inside the teenager

parts.note: a youth is a young person, a teenager
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: A teenager carrying a hidden weapon at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: Great Yarmouth is a seaside town in Norfolk, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarmouth is a resort on the English coast in Norfolk.
